item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is preferable because its retry implementation and tests directly exercise the reported os.Open case, and it preserves more of the existing Files option behavior. Both patches substantially violate the frozen contract and would require revision before merge.","reasons":["A tests retries with an actual *os.File and prevents net/http from closing the underlying seekable reader between attempts; B tests a strings.Reader wrapper and leaves req.Body as the original closer, risking failure when retrying an *os.File.","A’s retry test verifies both attempts contain identical complete multipart bytes. B checks only multipart metadata on retry and does not verify the file content was replayed.","A allows the established WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions constructors to affect Upload, whereas B introduces a separate request-option constructor and omits existing Files query handling.","A’s implementation is more thoroughly verified for fixed Content-Length, non-seekable behavior, multipart filename/field/content, validation, and replay."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required ...FilesOption.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating request, decoding, and error logic.","It adds explicitly prohibited association fields and an arbitrary form-field API, and extends multipartbody beyond the required NewFile helper usage intent visible in the contract wording about reuse of NewFile itself; more importantly, the association machinery is out of scope regardless of helper choice near it in the diff context. It also changes public option-constructor return types, creating avoidable API churn despite preserving ordinary call-site assignability in many cases; function values or explicit signature expectations can still be affected. The raw retry refactor globally changes closing and Content-Length semantics for seekable request bodies, which the contract expressly excludes. No test covers propagation of a source-reader failure."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong ...UploadFileOption signature and bypasses FilesService.Add.","It adds prohibited association APIs and unrelated global retry machinery.","ensureReplayableBody leaves the original seekable req.Body closeable; for *os.File, net/http may close it after the first attempt, causing the GetBody seek to fail. Its test deliberately uses a non-closing strings.Reader wrapper and therefore misses this case from the report. Upload also does not retain existing FilesOption query behavior. The retry test does not read and compare the uploaded content on both attempts, and no source-reader error test is included."]}
